question.text: Under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, Section 10 empowers which authority to authorize persons to deal in foreign exchange?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 10 of FEMA empowers RBI to authorize any person, on any application made to it, to deal in foreign exchange or foreign securities as an authorized dealer, money changer, offshore banking unit, or in such other manner as it considers fit. The Trap: SEBI regulates securities markets, but the authorization to deal in foreign exchange is specifically vested with RBI under FEMA. Note: The authorization route under Section 10 is the foundation for the entire AD / money-changer / OBU framework administered by RBI.
